editorial.exam_day_guidance: The exam is a 60-minute linear test consisting of 40 multiple-choice questions. You must achieve a passing score of 65% to earn the certification. Ensure you manage your time effectively across the three domains to address all questions within the allotted period.

faq.answer_text: The exam consists of 40 multiple-choice questions in total. Candidates should be prepared to answer these questions within the time limit provided, ensuring they cover all three domains of the syllabus to achieve the required passing score for certification.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: A passing score of 65% is required to pass the exam. This percentage reflects the minimum level of knowledge required to demonstrate proficiency in Agile testing principles, practices, and techniques as defined by the official ISTQB certification standards for this specific level.

The exam has a duration of 60 minutes. During this time, candidates must complete all 40 questions. It is recommended that test-takers manage their time carefully to ensure they have enough time to review their answers before the final submission of the test.

The approximate price is $250, though fees vary by national member board. Candidates should check with their local or regional ISTQB member board to confirm the exact pricing and registration procedures applicable to their specific location before scheduling their exam appointment.

editorial.meta_description: The CTFL-AT exam is scheduled for retirement on 2027-05-06. The ISTQB now recommends the Certified Tester Foundation Level (CTFL) as the official successor.

methodology.summary: This editorial was constructed using the official ISTQB syllabus and verified exam facts to provide a clear overview of the certification requirements and the transition to the CTFL successor, ensuring all information remains accurate and compliant with official documentation.

editorial.overview: The Foundation Level — Agile Tester (CTFL-AT) certification, provided by the ISTQB, covers testing principles and practices within Agile software development environments. It addresses the role of the tester in Agile teams, including test-driven development, user story creation, and the use of various testing tools. The exam evaluates knowledge across three specific domains, with the largest portion focusing on fundamental Agile testing principles, practices, and processes. This certification ensures that professionals understand the unique challenges and methodologies required to maintain high quality standards while working in fast-paced, iterative development cycles common in modern software engineering.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official ISTQB study documentation to understand the learning objectives for each domain. Focus on the 55% weight assigned to fundamental Agile testing principles. Practice identifying the differences between traditional and Agile testing, and ensure you are familiar with the terminology related to Agile methods, techniques, and tools. Use the provided syllabus to guide your study, as all content is examinable. Candidates should allocate sufficient time to master the core concepts and apply them to real-world scenarios.
editorial.who_should_take: This certification is for software testers and team members working in Agile environments. It is suitable for those who need to understand how to apply testing techniques, collaborate within a whole-team approach, and contribute to quality in iterative development projects.

exam_price_notes: $250 approximate; fees vary by national member board.
exam_rules: Closed-book. No notes or reference materials permitted. CTFL is the recommended prerequisite for all advanced and specialist levels. ISTQB certifications do not expire. Remote proctoring available in some countries; check with local member board.
id_requirements: Government-issued photo ID required. Name must match registration exactly. Requirements may vary by national member board.

lifecycle.summary: ISTQB retires CTFL-AT on 2027-05-06. CTFL is the named replacement path.
